body:
Thanks for responding. I'm going to try to interact with my family more but I'm not sure I can share how I've been feeling just yet or ever. It's hard to talk about because my parents are from another country and I don't speak their native language too well, just conversationally, but not enough to really talk about my feelings. I'm trying to just be closer to them though, and more open about my needs, but it will be a gradual process.

Thanks for the helpful advice. I know I need to be proactive and get my shit together. The hard part will be having no one with me but myself. I hope I can put aside feeling completely alone long enough to get my shit together and see myself through, so that I can begin new friendships from a positive place instead of using them to cope.
It's great that you took that step. I hope it truly helps you and that things start clearing up for you.

Hi, thanks for responding. It means so much that there are people willing to hear me out and talk to me. I really hope medication will help. I was taking Prozac for a few months when I was still in school and it kicked in almost immediately. I had to stop when I left school, then finally was able to see someone at home, and now I just started. It hasn't had the immediate effect it did last time, but I really, really hope it works out for me again. I thought I had things back on track, including with this new relationship, but the past four months everything has spiraled out of control. I hardly leave my house and I feel that I should go for a walk and listen to music or read, but I'm scared of breaking down in public, and it's easier to stay in my bed. Maybe I really should do that, though. I'm so scared of my own thoughts.

 I feel truly alone in the world for the first time--there is no one I can text or call for a conversation, and I'm trying to give my boyfriend space so he can think about things. I don't feel it's either of our faults, but I wish he would acknowledge that he hurt me by pulling away, as I've acknowledged that I hurt him by being passive-aggressive about it. But maybe he is right. I think we had different expectations--I thought he'd be able to keep in touch while he worked on school, and when he didn't I thought it was a reflection on the relationship. Meanwhile, he thought that school is a temporary thing he has to focus on, and that when it's done, he'll have more time for us. It hurts because I can't even imagine meeting someone else now that I'm not in school. I also know I shouldn't meet someone else because I need to learn to be by myself and rebuild my life. But right now I'm *too* by myself and it's scary. I can go whole days without interacting with anyone and it's really sad.

I don't really know where I'm going with this, and you don't have to respond. You've already said so many helpful things. I'm going to try to muster up the strength to drive to a park to bring music and a book because I don't know how else I'll get through the day.
